title: Piercing Statue Solo #130 (힙컷 · P100 정의형 · 몸통 3조각 · 왼팔 석재(black granite) · 오른팔 목재(purpleheart) · 몸통 [세로 3등분] 내용물(사파이어+나비) / 투명(스모키 블랙 유리) / 석재(lapis lazuli) · 왼허벅지 목재(purpleheart) · 오른허벅지 수조(내용물 물) · 체형 still-visible cinched waist beneath · 탑노트 · 비비드바이올렛 · 메이크업 히메갸루 · 금속 로즈골드 · 쥬얼리 목걸이·헤어 장식·반지 JQ4)
prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut statue multi-material portrait: real face and neck, and a sculpted body made of different materials — her left arm carved stone, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (solid glass holding embedded objects, clear crystal and carved stone), her left thigh carved wood and her right thigh a glass vessel full of water. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually rounded, deliberately carved tips a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end at her thighs, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Japanese woman — fair porcelain skin, soft pink blush across the cheeks, sparkling pink eyeshadow, long curled lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, glossy candy-pink lips, a sweet princess-like smile, bold vivid violet-purple hair styled in a high top-knot bun. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Her neck, the hollows above her collarbones and the tops of her shoulders carry the same real living skin as her face: visible pores and fine skin grain, a soft sheen of natural skin oils on the highest planes, faint fine peach-fuzz hairs catching the rim light, gentle tonal variation with a natural warm flush, and the fine natural creases of a real neck — never airbrushed, never smooth like plastic. Like any real person she is slightly asymmetrical: a few small natural beauty marks and freckles scattered unevenly, one side of her neck and shoulder very slightly warmer and more freckled than the other.

Piercings: An extreme, dense armour of about one hundred real rose-gold piercings with a few rose-gold coin drops among them covering the face: a thick rose-gold septum ring with a smaller ring above it and two rose-gold rings through each nostril; a straight rose-gold bar across the bridge of the nose between the brows; five rose-gold pieces in a row along the outer half of each eyebrow, alternating small rings that pass through the brow skin with the skin visible through each loop and small round ball studs sitting on the skin; two rows of four small rose-gold studs across the forehead above the brows; four small studs up each temple on the bone, well clear of the eyes; a row of six small studs along each cheekbone; a rose-gold Medusa stud above the lips; a big rose-gold hoop, two smaller rings and a snake-bite ring on each side through the lower lip's edge, and five small hoops along the upper lip's edge; a rose-gold labret stud and four rings through the chin; five small studs along each jaw; on each ear a full dense row of ten oversized hoops, thick bars, stretched plugs, helix rings and studs from lobe to top, the biggest hoops hanging clear of the neck down to the shoulders; and eight fine rose-gold chains looping from the ear hoops to the nostril rings and the septum ring. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. All jewelry is real rose gold, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Jewelry: besides the piercings she wears seven to ten pieces, heavily stacked of rose-gold necklaces and chains resting on her neck, collarbones and upper chest; seven to ten pieces, heavily stacked of rose-gold hair ornaments set in her hair; seven to ten pieces, heavily stacked of rose-gold rings on her fingers, all of it real, sitting on and over the material of her body and her real neck and hair without covering her eyes, her face or her piercings.

Physique: A still-visible cinched waist beneath a full soft chest, wide curving hips, both thighs clearly separate and individually shaped, her left arm carved stone, her right arm carved wood, her torso split into three pieces (solid glass holding embedded objects, clear crystal and carved stone), her left thigh carved wood and her right thigh a glass vessel full of water.

Boundary (skin to material, at underarm height): A single straight, horizontal line runs across her body at underarm height, level with both armpits. Real skin above this line — her face, neck, both shoulders, and the very tops of both upper arms. Below this line, completely different materials meet at her body's natural joints (both shoulders, both hips) and at the seams inside the torso, each keeping its own distinct appearance right up to where it touches its neighbour, never blending into it. At the underarm line itself, the material immediately below rises in a small raised step above her skin, casting a crisp shadow. Shards interlock along this line only.

Left arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of polished black granite with fine silver flecks and a deep mirror-like sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same stone. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Right arm (shoulder to hand): carved from ONE solid block of deep violet purpleheart wood, a dense hardwood of rich purple with fine straight grain, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, every wrist, palm, finger and knuckle the same wood, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Torso (underarm line down to where the thighs begin): The torso, from the underarm line down to where the thighs begin, is divided into 3 side-by-side pieces by 2 straight vertical seams, about 33% and 57% of the way across it from the left of the picture to the right. Torso piece 1 (the piece on the left of the picture, left of the first seam): carved from ONE solid block of deep blue sapphire crystal, with fine silky needle inclusions forming a soft star-like shimmer, near-midnight navy where thickest and pale cornflower at every thin edge, never hollow, never split; suspended deep within it, visible through it like objects frozen inside a single flawless crystal, are a dozen small, perfectly carved crystal butterflies with delicate translucent wings, each one a paler, brighter facet than the crystal around it, each one fully embedded in the solid material with no cavity and no liquid around it. Light passes through the solid material; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. Torso piece 2 (the middle piece, between the two seams): solid transparent material, solid smoky black cast glass, with smoky depth with slow swirls and faint bubbles, hard mirror highlights, darkest where thickest, one continuous carved mass, never hollow. Light passes straight through it; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it. Torso piece 3 (the piece on the right of the picture, right of the second seam): carved from ONE solid block of deep lapis lazuli, a rich royal-blue stone scattered with small glittering flecks of golden pyrite throughout, polished to a hard, cool sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface.

Left thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): carved from ONE solid block of deep violet purpleheart wood, a dense hardwood of rich purple with fine straight grain, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, the grain running unbroken through it. No light passes through it — only reflections on its polished surface. The left thigh ends in its own smooth, deeply polished rounded tip, finished the way a carved sculpture is finished.

Right thigh (hip down to its tip, a short way down her thighs, just below the hip line): a sculpted vessel of the same clear glass (unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections, sharp white highlights, tiny trapped bubbles), completely filled to the brim with clear water holding a scattered handful of pale pink cherry-blossom petals drifting slowly inside it, never crowding, mostly open clear water around each one. It curves inward and seals shut into its own smooth, rounded, closed tip, the water continuing unbroken down to that tip. Light passes through; the backdrop is visibly bent inside it.

Where each material meets its neighbour (left shoulder, right shoulder, left hip, right hip, and every seam inside the torso), the two distinct materials sit flush against each other with a thin, clean seam, deliberate and precise, never jagged, torn or blended — always the finish of a sculpture, each material keeping its own colour, clarity and surface completely separate from the one beside it. Both thighs stay clearly separate all the way down, never merging into a single base, both rounded tips resting side by side on the surface beneath her.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a deep crimson on one side and a warm gold on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle — glowing evenly, marked with a few thin dark vertical lines so the bending of those lines is visible wherever the body is transparent, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, body angled 45 degrees, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body with the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so a deep crimson light glances off the left half and a warm gold light glances off the right half — passing straight through the transparent parts (right thigh, torso piece 1, torso piece 2), while only reflecting off the opaque parts (left arm, right arm, left thigh, torso piece 3). A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears. Shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
